edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber I 9

source_text: Nisi cognoveris te, o pulchra inter mulieres, egredere et abi post vestigia gregum, et pasce haedos tuos iuxta tabernacula pastorum. Cognitio sui principium est reversionis ad Deum. Si se nescierit sponsa, inter haedos — non oves — pascetur et a sponso separabitur. Pulchra inter mulieres: ecclesia inter animas, vel anima inter virtutes.
pass_a_gloss: Unless you-will-have-known yourself, O beautiful among women, go-out and depart after tracks of-flocks, and pasture goats your beside tents of-shepherds. Knowledge of-self beginning is of-return unto God...
pass_b_english: [[If you do not know yourself, O beautiful among women, go out and follow the tracks of the flocks, and pasture your goats beside the shepherds’ tents >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:8]]. Knowledge of oneself is the beginning of return to God. If the Bride does not know herself, she will pasture among goats — not sheep — and be separated from the Bridegroom. Beautiful among women: the church among souls, or the soul among virtues.
